transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Amy Held.
The Supreme Court has agreed to take up President Trump's executive order suspending asylum
at the southern border.
The Trump administration wants the high court to overturn lower court decisions that found
the ban unlawful.
Federal law allows people to ask for asylum if they fear persecution.
The ban was part of Trump's hardline immigration stance when he took office last year.
Federal prosecutors have filed a new indictment against the man accused of trying to assassinate
Trump last April at the White House Correspondents Dinner.
NPR's Ryan Lucas reports.
The new indictment adds one count of committing an act of terrorism while armed.
That's in addition to the other counts Cole Allen was already facing, including trying
to assassinate President Trump.
He has pleaded not guilty.
Researchers say Allen traveled from Los Angeles to Washington, D.C. and booked a room in the
same hotel where the White House Correspondents Dinner was taking place in April.
He then allegedly tried to storm the dinner with a shotgun and other weapons to kill President
Trump, but was stopped by Secret Service agents at the outer perimeter.
Ryan Lucas, NPR News, Washington.
Microsoft says it is seeing encouraging recovery progress in Europe and improvements in North
America following a major global outage.
Ms. Mee Nicholson has this report.
Microsoft attributes the outage to elevated load on its server infrastructure, saying
there is currently no sign of malicious activity.
The outage has shut down email, teams and co-pilot across the globe, impacting other
tech providers, including open AI and anthropic, and forcing businesses and governments to
resort to older tech, including fax machines.
European stock exchange operator Euronext instructed listed companies to pick up the telephone.
European Group Mask issued the same advice to its customers.
The outage is prompting fresh calls within the EU to control its own digital infrastructure
and reduce dependency on U.S. servers and providers.
For NPR News, I'm Ms. Mee Nicholson in Berlin.
Scientists have created a map of the part of the brain implicated in diseases like schizophrenia
and Alzheimer's.
NPR's Ping Huang has this report.
The basal ganglia are a set of interconnected brain structures tucked beneath the cerebral
cortex.
Hong Kui Zen, director of brain science at the Allen Institute, says they're key to
some important brain functions.
Including movement control, decision making, habit formation, as well as reward and emotion.
They're also key to some psychiatric disorders and diseases that affect the nervous system.
So over three years, with funding from the National Institutes of Health, she and colleagues
at more than 50 research institutions came together to create a cellular atlas of the
different cell types and the basal ganglia across humans and primates.
The results are out in more than two dozen papers published by Cell Press.
The next step, she says, is to map the whole brain.
Ping Huang, NPR News.
This is NPR News.
The head coach of the U.S. men's national soccer team is headed to England.
Mauricio Pochettino, who led the squad through last summer's FIFA World Cup, has taken a
job with Manchester United.
NPR's Becky Sullivan has more.
In 2024, the U.S. men's national soccer team was flagging, just as a golden opportunity
of a World Cup co-hosted here at home was around the corner.
So U.S. soccer swung big and hired the highest profile coach to ever lead the team, Mauricio
Pochettino, the big name manager who turned around Tottenham Hotspur and went on to lead
some of Europe's most famous clubs like Chelsea and PSG.
In two years, Pochettino revamped the player pool and led the U.S. men's team to three
wins at the World Cup before their exit in the round of 16.
Afterward, in August, Pochettino signed a new four-year contract with U.S. soccer, but said
Friday that there are few opportunities in a coaching career like Manchester United,
one of the most historic clubs in English soccer.
Becky Sullivan, NPR News.
A Kansas district attorney says he will not file charges against the driver in a deadly
crash at a crowded Wichita soccer field last month.
That crash left two people dead, including a six-year-old and 10 other people injured.
A police investigation finds the driver fell asleep at the wheel and did not act with intent
or recklessness.
SpaceX is launching its massive Starship rocket again from Texas today with the aim of recapturing
the entire rocket a double catch, the massive booster, followed days later by the spacecraft.
If successful, it would be a first.
The 14 previous Starships ended up in the ocean, either by design or by accident, in
a stream of flaming wreckage.
This is NPR News.

topics.text: Supreme Court agrees to hear Trump's executive order suspending asylum at southern border
Federal prosecutors file new terrorism indictment against Cole Allen over April assassination attempt on Trump
Microsoft reports recovery progress after global outage that disrupted email, Teams, and Copilot
Scientists map basal ganglia cell types across humans and primates, relevant to schizophrenia and Alzheimer's
Mauricio Pochettino leaves U.S. men's national soccer team to coach Manchester United
Kansas prosecutor declines charges against driver in deadly Wichita soccer field crash
SpaceX launches Starship from Texas aiming for first-ever recapture of booster and spacecraft
